title: Parametric, Polar, and Complex Representations
description: For x=2t-1 and y=t^2, -2≤t≤3, find endpoints, direction, and the Cartesian curve.
outcomes: Interpret x=f(t), y=g(t) as a directed path with a parameter interval.
Eliminate parameters while preserving interval restrictions and lost orientation information.
Use r(t)=<x(t),y(t)> to describe position, displacement, and average velocity.
Distinguish curve intersections from self-intersections and repeated positions.
Represent points as (r,theta), use negative radius, and generate equivalent polar coordinates.
Convert points and equations using x=r cos theta, y=r sin theta, and r^2=x^2+y^2.
Trace r=f(theta) using tables, signed radius, and interval selection.
Test symmetry and choose intervals that trace a polar curve exactly once.
Analyze parameter effects in circles, cardioids, limacons, roses, lemniscates, spirals, and conics.
Represent complex numbers by modulus and argument and convert between rectangular and polar forms.
Multiply moduli, add arguments, divide moduli, subtract arguments, and apply De Moivre's theorem.
Find all nth roots of a complex number and interpret their equal angular spacing.
